candidates.exact_span: According to the Forum-adopted NPDES permit program policies (for Municipal Discharges), in order for a permittee to be in compliance with the Forum's municipal discharges criteria, the incremental increase in salinity shall be 400 mg/L or less, which is considered to be a reasonable incremental increase above the flow weighted average salinity of the intake water supply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the default numeric salinity/TDS incremental-increase compliance threshold and the intake-flow-weighted baseline methodology; different readings of 'incremental increase in salinity,' 'flow weighted average salinity of the intake water supply,' or applicability of Forum municipal criteria would change which enforceable limit is assigned for comparison to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: However, the permitting authority may permit a discharge in excess of the 400 mg/L incremental increase at the time of issuance or reissuance of a NPDES discharge permit, upon satisfactory demonstration by the permittee that it is not practicable to attain the 400 mg/L limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when a higher-than-400 mg/L numeric limit may be authorized; interpretation of 'practicable,' timing at issuance/reissuance, and whether a satisfactory demonstration was made affects whether the 400 mg/L default or an alternative numeric limit governs compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: April 10, 2015, the facility demonstrated that it was economically impractical to attain the net 400 mg/L incremental increase limit at that time. Because of that demonstration, EPA allowed a temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L for the previous permit cycle,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies a prior-cycle enforceable numeric limit (497 mg/L as a 30-day average TDS net incremental increase) and the economic-impracticability basis for departing from 400 mg/L; whether that limit applied during FY2025-relevant periods or only the prior cycle changes which numeric limit is used for exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: provided that the facility will diligently control and reduce TDS in their discharge (i.e., maintaining the formulated BMP activities, monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis, and completing $14 million upgrades at the WWTP to improve overall effluent quality (i.e., reducing TDS in their discharges)).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ties permit authorization to ongoing BMP maintenance, regular effluent quality and quantity monitoring, and upgrade completion; interpretation of whether these conditions created independent monitoring obligations or affected when monitoring was required would change monitoring-applicability findings.

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington has constructed a new sampling station where water intake samplings have been conducted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intake sampling underpins net incremental TDS/salinity limit derivation and may establish intake-monitoring expectations; whether intake samples were required, where they must be taken, and whether they are available affects both the calculated applicable limit (Purpose A) and whether intake monitoring was an applicable obligation (Purpose B).

candidates.exact_span: EPA believes the TDS data collected during the past permit cycle are sufficient and representative of facility existing operation conditions and can be used to derive the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that past-cycle TDS data will be used to derive the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit; disagreement over sufficiency, representativeness, or derivation method would change the numeric limit selected for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: EPA cannot grant the permittee request of keeping the temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Rejects continuation of the 497 mg/L limit in the draft permit, implying a different final numeric limit will apply; interpretation of whether this governs the reissued permit during FY2025 changes which limit is enforceable for measurement comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: To protect and maintain existing water quality as required by 40 CFR §122(4)(d) and to prevent further degradation of water quality in the San Juan River in accordance with 40 CFR §131.12, Subsection A of 20.6.4.8 NMAC, the New Mexico Continuing Planning Process –
candidates.computation_change_reason: Invokes antidegradation and continuing-planning authorities as the basis for not retaining 497 mg/L, but the sentence is truncated in this segment; how these provisions constrain the final limit or evidence needed to justify limit changes is incomplete, leaving uncertainty that could affect both the applicable numeric limit (Purpose A) and whether missing or incomplete supporting evidence leaves limit applicability unresolved (Purpose C).
